# Parallel final carry normalization

**Component gate failed; no full-proof integration is admitted.** Intended Fq/R256 geometric candidate/control ratios are 1.012644 versus accepted (0/31 blocks) and 1.012687 versus fresh OFF (0/31). These are component measurements; production source is unchanged.

## Change and correctness argument

Only native eight-lane CIOS multiplication's final normalization changes. All product and cancellation steps retain their accepted implementation. Write each lower coefficient as t_j = r_j + B*q_j for B=2^52. Transfer each q_j to coefficient j+1 simultaneously. This preserves the represented integer exactly, while avoiding the common serial carry chain.

The low coefficient is already normalized. Only coefficients 1–3 can still exceed B-1; the bitwise OR of those coefficients exceeds B-1 exactly when any does. If that happens in any lane, ripple all three coefficients to handle cascades of arbitrary length. The top word retains the same unrestricted role as in the original normalization. Correctness does not assume random inputs or rare carries.

CIOS coefficients receive at most six IFMA product/reduction half terms per row. Five rows and the small carried words remain conservatively below 31B. Final mixed-radix repacking shifts at most four bits, remaining below 512B=2^61. The new first pass adds at most 511 to a lower masked digit or top word; correction adds at most one. No u64 overflow is possible under that bound. Direct coefficient tests cover the broader [0,2^61) domain.

The [DigitsOnTurbo paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.21566v1#S3.SS1) separates ordinary carries from cascading carries. This independently written adaptation operates across five radix-52 vectors, each holding independent fields. It is not a port of the paper's saturated-word integer routine, and its reported speedups are not transferred here. The paper was reviewed earlier; this normalization implementation is new. The failed truncated-Montgomery experiments remain failed.

No heap, lookup tables, key preparation or storage-layout changes are introduced. There is no extra inverse constant. Four-lane production, field add/sub, reduction bounds and all consumers retain their implementation. Temporary register liveness and stack use still matter.

## Component measurements

Ryzen 9950X, one thread pinned to CPU 2, 31 rotating/reversing process blocks. Each process performs three 2,000-iteration primes and 100,000 measured iterations. All 32 canonical output fields match across all controls/blocks per case. No owned build/profile/other benchmark overlaps timing.

Values are ns per field lane per iteration; streams4 additionally divides by four. Curve-update is a dependent field expression, not a full curve operation. The butterfly produces two outputs. Input construction and output checking are outside timing; packing within the butterfly loop is included.

All 20 cases must remain within 3% pooled of both controls; fresh OFF must remain within 3% of accepted. There is no minimum gain floor or unchanged reroll. Calibration passed: True; all-pattern nonregression passed: False.

## Validation and code generation

The independent integer model passes 158,304 normalization cases at radices 2^4, 2^8 and 2^52, including exhaustive boundary combinations, random coefficients and cascading carries. Native OFF and ON each pass 35 field tests. New direct SIMD normalization checks cover 81,920 lane outputs across four/eight lanes, including zero through three cascading steps. The retained 415,888 Arkworks comparisons rerun across two primes, two radices, ordinary/fused/difference arithmetic, lazy bounds and eight-step chains. Generator consistency passes.

Static instruction counts include the cold correction path; they are not executed counts. Stack operands include ordinary temporaries as well as spills. Only standalone wrappers are counted, not full prover kernels.

The first native build failed because the generated eight-lane test retained an explicit four-lane vector type. The source and error are preserved under evidence/initial-failures/test-vector-type. Removing that test annotation allowed type inference at both widths; arithmetic and timing criteria were unchanged, and no timing had run.

There are 1,860 timed observations, zero SDK proofs and zero independent Gnark exports. Full proof latency and portable/API/finite-pressure/concurrency qualification are still required before adoption. No AWS, Aeglos, mobile or giant-circuit result follows. Accepted primary remains 9.153 ms and 54→1 228.911 ms. All original eight shapes still miss the supplied M5 CPU 10× target.
